facts.text: Dwight, Nebraska was founded in 1887 when the Fremont, Elkhorn and Missouri Valley Railroad reached the area, named after Dwight, Illinois, the hometown of its first postmaster.
Czech and Bohemian immigrants arriving in the late 1860s laid the cultural foundation of Dwight, with their traditions still evident in local institutions and a Czech Catholic cemetery.
The Assumption Catholic Church, built starting in 1931, features a central fountain and a shrine to the Virgin Mary and was listed on the National Register in 2008.
